subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Beyond Prospect Theory: What Comes Next
description: A quick, practical guide to Beyond Prospect Theory: What Comes Next.

hook.text: Prospect theory is 45 years old. Is it still the best description of how we decide? New models are emerging.

buildup.text: Cumulative prospect theory, regret theory, and the query theory each address gaps in the original framework.

discovery.text: But prospect theory's core insights hold: reference points, loss aversion, and probability weighting still dominate.

twist.text: Neuroscience now confirms the S-curve. Brain regions respond to gains and losses exactly as the theory predicts.

climax.text: The best model is the one that changes how you see your own choices. Prospect theory does that better than any rival.

punchline.text: Know the curve. Then decide despite it.

quiz.question: What are prospect theory's most enduring insights?
options: Reference points, loss aversion, and probability weighting
Emotions have no role in decision-making

details.summary: Researchers are extending prospect theory by incorporating emotions, social context, and neural processes into decision models. Neuroeconomics and computational approaches aim to explain the biological mechanisms behind the biases prospect theory describes.
details.whyItMatters: Prospect theory explains what people do but not fully why. Next-generation models integrating brain science and social factors promise more precise predictions and better-designed policies for improving decisions.
takeaways: Neuroeconomics maps brain activity during gain and loss processing
Social context and emotions are being integrated into decision models
Computational models simulate prospect theory at the neural level

faq.question: What has brain scanning revealed about loss aversion?
faq.answer: Brain imaging shows that losses activate the amygdala and other threat-processing regions more intensely than equivalent gains activate reward centers. This neural asymmetry provides biological evidence for prospect theory's core insight.

faq.question: Will prospect theory be replaced by a better model?
faq.answer: More likely refined than replaced. Prospect theory's core insights about reference dependence and loss aversion are robust. Future models will add precision by explaining individual differences and contextual variation.
